implementation_notes: Python expresses optional named settings directly: parameters after `*` are keyword-only and can carry defaults (`def connect(host, *, timeout=30.0, tls=True)`), so a caller names only what changes and the required list never grows; typing tools and IDEs see every option. Where the option set is large, shared between functions or must be serialized, a frozen dataclass with `kw_only=True` fields turns it into an inspectable value and `dataclasses.replace` derives modified configurations; `functools.partial` pre-binds a base configuration for reuse. The wildcard `**kwargs` form is the anti-pattern: it hides option names, defeats type checkers and turns typos into silently ignored settings.
pitfalls: `**kwargs` is not an options API: option names become invisible to IDEs and type checkers, misspellings are silently ignored, and the documented defaults have to be reimplemented by hand.

Mutable default values are evaluated once at function definition (`def f(acc=[])`), so a mutable option default is shared across all calls; use `None` sentinels or `field(default_factory=...)` in dataclasses.

Keyword-only defaults only help callers who use the names: inserting a parameter before the `*` still breaks positional callers, so keep required parameters stable and put every optional setting after `*`.

variants.name: Frozen keyword-only dataclass as an options object
variants.implementation_notes: A frozen dataclass with `kw_only=True` fields makes the option set a value: construction stays named with keyword-only defaults, and the object can additionally be inspected (`dataclasses.asdict`), compared, hashed, serialized and derived (`dataclasses.replace(opts, tls=True)`). Choose it when options outgrow a signature, are passed through several layers, or must be logged or persisted; keyword-only parameters remain the simpler default for a handful of settings, and dataclasses require Python 3.7 (kw_only: 3.10).
variants.code_sketch:
from dataclasses import dataclass, replace

@dataclass(frozen=True, kw_only=True)
class Options:
    host: str = "localhost"
    port: int = 8080
    tls: bool = False

cfg = Options(port=9000)
derived = replace(cfg, tls=True)
pitfalls: `frozen=True` prevents attribute assignment but not mutation of mutable field values (a list field can still be appended to); use tuples or `default_factory` with immutable values.
`dataclasses.replace` re-runs `__init__`/`__post_init__`, so validation runs again and `init=False` fields are not carried over unless `__post_init__` reconstructs them.
A dataclass options object is a new type in every signature: callers must import it, and defaults defined on the class are easy to duplicate in a second 'defaults' constant that then drifts.
